He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==High school career== Stanley first attended [[Harvard-Westlake School]] in [[Studio City, Los Angeles|Studio City, California]]. As a sophomore, Stanley averaged 17.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game. In 2017, Stanley transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, California]] for his last two years of high school.{{Cite news|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/2019-five-star-cassius-stanley-transferring-to-sierra-canyon-calif|title=2019 five-star Cassius Stanley transferring to Sierra Canyon (Calif.)|last=|first=|date=|work=www.usatodayhss.com|access-date=June 8, 2017}} As a senior, he averaged 17.8 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 2.9 assists per game while leading the Sierra Canyon to a 32–3 overall record. ===Recruiting=== On April 22, 2019, Stanley committed to play at [[Duke University]].{{cite edges third-ranked Kansas 68-66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168155 |accessdate=November 5, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} After injuring his leg in a victory over [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]] on November 29, Stanley was ruled out indefinitely.{{cite news |title=Duke's Cassius Stanley exits Winthrop game with left leg injury |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28190795/duke-cassius-stanley-exits-winthrop-game-left-leg-injury |accessdate=November 30, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=November 29, 2019}} However, after his leg improved quicker than expected due to rehabilitation and physical therapy, he returned to play against [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] after missing just one game.{{cite news |last1=Wiseman |first1=Steve |title=How Duke basketball’s Cassius Stanley returned so quickly |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/article238129364.html |accessdate=December 31, 2019 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=December 6, 2019}} On January 4, Stanley scored 20 points and 5 rebounds in a 95–62 win over [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168355|title=Carey scores 24 to lead No.2 Duke past Miami|publisher=ESPN|date=January 4, 2020|access-date=January 4, 2020}} On February 8, Stanley recorded 22 points and 6 rebounds in a 98–96 overtime victory over rival [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168364|title=Jones, Moore help No.7 Duke top rival UNC 98–96 in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=February 8, 2020|access-date=February 8, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Stanley was selected to the ACC All-Freshman Team.{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men’s Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|accessdate=March 9, 2020}} Stanley averaged 12.6 points and 4.9 rebounds per game, shooting 47 percent from the floor and 36 percent shooting from three-point range. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Duke’s Cassius Stanley enters 2020 NBA draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/04/07/cassius-stanley/ |accessdate=April 7, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=April 7, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] | 29 || 29 || 27.4 || .474 || .360 || .733 || 4.9 || 1.0 || .7 || .7 || 12.6 {{S-end}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211806498&DB_OEM_ID=4200&Q_SEASON=2019 Duke Blue Devils bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Stanley, Cassius}} [[Category:1999 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:African-American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from California]] [[Category:Duke Blue Devils men's basketball players]] [[Category:Harvard-Westlake School alumni]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sierra Canyon School alumni]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Los Angeles]]
